It will be mostly an overview with pointers to articles that dissect various problems in more detail. Most of these articles are freely available online. 1.5.1 Mal’tsev term Definition 1.5.1. We say that p(x, y, z) is a Mal’tsev term if • p(x, x, y) = y • p(x, y, y) = x. An example of a Mal’tsev term would be the p operation on binary algebras, in a general group we could take p(x, y, z) = xy −1 z. Theorem 1.5.2. If A has a Mal’tsev term then CSP(A) is in P.
